why: Close to a guess in a badly fragmented 30-cluster event: I take 16005 because a 24.8 cm prong cools into it with a monotone Bragg rise to 220k at 16001 and a second prong rises from it to a 148k proton peak 5 cm out, but the event's only clean 3-of-3 rule-1 candidate 80062 is merely tier-dropped by its 153 degree prong pair rather than eliminated, and the busy 16007/16016 knot 8 cm away is a live alternative.

Rule 1 plus rule 2: the only real object is a 94.9 cm muon whose sharp 490k Bragg spike (dark red in the zoom) is at the 9000 end, so it cools toward 9003, which is also the lowest-z candidate at z=19.5 and carries a second 4.8 cm prong at 126 degrees.

Rule 3 disqualifies 14002 (stopping-muon Bragg to 140k with a 7 cm Michel stub), leaving the muon start; the muon line extrapolated forward from 14000 passes within 0.7 cm of 48017 in all three projections, where a 15.4 cm 200-335k proton begins, so the junction sits at the proton start rather than 4.3 cm back at 14000.

Rule 1 satisfied 2 of 2: the 160 cm MIP track cools into 14002 with a monotone Bragg to 140k at the far end 14001, and the 16 cm 2.5-3x MIP proton also cools into it; the zoom shows an abrupt orange-to-green dQ/dx discontinuity at the 132 degree kink, so these are two particles, not one scattered track.

Rule 1 at a degree-5 star with zero prongs rising toward it: a 7.3 cm proton stops at 162k and a 19.9 cm prong rises x4.3 to 116k, and three further objects converge on it - cluster 85's 15 cm MIP muon at 10.4 cm and cluster 87's EM shower apex at 12.0 cm both point straight back at this point (rule 7).

The best raw rule-1 candidate 3002 is the collinearity trap in its extreme form - its two hot prongs are 180 degrees apart and the zoom shows one smooth continuous track through it with no kink and no colour step - so the vertex is the upstream 3-prong junction 3006, whose prongs are 116/117/127 degrees apart with an 8.2 cm stub stopping at 174k, and which rule 2 also prefers.

Rule 8 event with nothing to read: three isolated sub-centimetre blips, no segments, no direction, no p2/p4 panels. 27002 sits in a detector corner, so the only plausible pair is 23000 and 60004 11 cm apart, and rule 2 is the sole available discriminator - 23000 is upstream at z=387.2 against z=396.2.

Trap 1 verbatim - two Bragg ends in one cluster, a wide template-matching stopping-muon rise to 210k at 3001 and a sharp 3.5 cm 320k terminus at 3000 - so I take the junction they both point away from, with rule 1 scoring 2 of 2 there; the 171.5 degree prong pair costs it one confidence tier.

Close to a guess: the event is two disconnected faint structures, a 26 cm track ending in a 145k spike at 4000 and an EM shower apex at 52037 whose backward axis does not point at that track, 27 cm apart across an empty gap; only 4002 and 52045 have a prong rising away with none rising toward, and 52045's prongs are 153 degrees collinear, so I take 4002 on rule 1 plus rule 2.

Rule 1 at a 3-prong junction in the biggest cluster and at the event's lowest z: two prongs stop away from it (a 12.6 cm rise to 165k at 17001 and a 27.1 cm arm that is near zero at 17003 and 92k at 17002) and a 140k blob sits within 2 cm of the vertex; the 164 degree pair 17001-17003-17002 costs one tier.

Rule 1 on a single 128 cm track whose dQ/dx climbs monotonically 55k-54k-84k-107k-145k-202k along the chain, so it cools all the way toward 7001, which is also the lowest-z candidate; the track runs upward in y, which is what rules out an entering cosmic, and the rules forbid screening out a wall-touching cluster anyway.

The only cluster in the event, rule 1 scores 2 of 2 at its only junction, and p4 independently template-matches a terminal Bragg on each arm (a 250k-to-55k proton-template decline from 13000 and a rise to 210k on the stopping-muon template at 13001); one particle cannot produce two terminal Braggs, both free ends are rule-1 negative, and the 147.8 degree prong pair is below the 150 degree collinearity threshold so no tier drop applies.

Rule 1 plus rule 2 at the lowest-z point of the 224 cm cluster: the X-Y zoom shows two distinct point trails diverging from 18006 at 31 degrees, both cool there (36k and 50k) and both getting hotter away, one stopping at 92k after 35 cm and the other stopping at 120k after 182 cm, while the competing junctions 18005 and 18002 are 176 and 167 degree collinear fit breaks.

Rule 1 at a sharp 80 degree V with a clean dQ/dx discontinuity in the zoom: a cyan MIP 75.7 cm track on one arm and a dark-red 12.7 cm proton peaking at 205k on the other, which unambiguously starts at 8003; the more upstream alternative 8001 is only a track terminus with zero prongs rising away, and rule 2 is a tie-break that must not overturn that.
